title: Active incidence and comma-cone comparisons for operadic families
statement:
Use the small families, their fiberwise inert edges and incidence cones of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence], monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and coherent functors of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $n\geq1$ and $\pi:\mathcal P\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n$ be a family whose restrictions to all parameter edges are constant over $[0]$ and whose zero-fibers are spaces. Require the inert lifts over $(\alpha,\operatorname{id}_t)$ to be $\pi$-cocartesian in the whole family, not only cocartesian after restriction to a parameter fiber; these are the stationary inert lifts used below. Put $\mathcal A=\mathcal P_0$. For an object $b\in\mathcal P_t$, $t>0$, put $J_b=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal P}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{act}})_{/b}$. For a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^d\to\mathcal P_{\{1,\ldots,n\}}$ consisting of active arrows, define $X_\sigma=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal P}\mathcal P_{/\sigma}$: its $k$-simplices are maps $\Delta^k\star\Delta^d\to\mathcal P$ equal to $\sigma$ on the last factor and lying in $\mathcal A$ on the first factor. Let $X_\sigma^{\mathrm a}\subseteq X_\sigma$ require every mixed edge from the first factor to the first vertex of $\sigma$ to be active.

(i) If $b$ lies over $[r]$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ are its consecutive inert edge restrictions, cutting the source tuple along the inert projections gives an equivalence $J_b\simeq\prod_{i=1}^rJ_{b_i}$. For every inert-preserving $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ this equivalence identifies the source diagram, together with its base map to $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, with concatenation of the source diagrams on the $J_{b_i}$. These comparisons also identify induced cones whenever the inert projections of $b$ and of their source tuples are preserved. For $r=0$, $J_b$ is contractible and its source diagram is the empty tuple. These comparisons include the common endpoints of adjacent inputs; no discreteness of the zero-fibers is required.

(ii) Restriction to the first vertex gives a trivial Kan fibration $X_\sigma^{\mathrm a}\to J_{\sigma(0)}$. Here trivial Kan fibration means right lifting against every simplicial boundary, including dimension zero.

(iii) Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ be inert-preserving and $f:X_\sigma\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ its composite with source evaluation. For a diagram $g:T\to E$, write $E_{g/}$ for the join coslice, whose $k$-simplices are extensions $T\star\Delta^k\to E$ of $g$. With $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $f^{\mathrm a}=f|_{X_\sigma^{\mathrm a}}$, the restriction map
$$ (\mathcal V^\otimes)_{f/}\longrightarrow(\mathcal V^\otimes)_{f^{\mathrm a}/}\times_{(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})_{pf^{\mathrm a}/}}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})_{pf/} $$
is a trivial Kan fibration. Thus prescribed simplices and all their boundaries in these coslices lift with exactly the specified base and restrictions. This compares only these source-comma diagrams with their active parts; it does not identify an operadic colimit with a colimit relative to the whole projection $p$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp. 336–337: active-part coslice comparison, restriction to the first vertex, and the product over inert outputs. GH Theorem A.3.4 specifies the generalized nonsymmetric extension: use incidence diagrams including endpoints, with the constant Kan zero-fiber condition. Nonsymmetric formulation following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178v4 Appendix A. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact. Family convention checked against HA Definition 2.3.2.10(a): inert lifts stationary in the parameter are cocartesian for the whole family projection. The explicit global condition is needed for the active-source reflection, not inferred from the fiberwise condition alone.
